D-wave等实现双轨擦除量子比特纠缠门
本研究针对编码于超导微波腔对中的双轨擦除量子比特，设计并实现了双比特纠缠门。实验表明，该门（约500 ns）基本保持了误差层级，擦除率约0.5%，残余泡利误差低于0.1%，且比特翻转误差极低（10⁻⁶）。表面码模拟证实，该方案为纠错系统提供快速抑制误差的扩展路径。该工作为实用化容错量子计算提供了关键进展。研究成果于8月5日发表于《Nature》（自然）。
来源：
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10822-y
DARPA启动“It’s About Time”项目，以建立光学钟的试点制造流程

# Weekly Report | D-Wave Achieves High-Fidelity Entangling Gate for Dual-Rail Erasure Qubits in 500 ns; DARPA Fires Opening Shot in "Quantum Manufacturing" with Launch of "It's About Time" Program…

---

## D-Wave et al. Realize Entangling Gate for Dual-Rail Erasure Qubits

This study designs and demonstrates a two-qubit entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits encoded in pairs of superconducting microwave cavities. Experiments show that the gate (~500 ns) largely preserves the error hierarchy: the erasure rate is approximately 0.5%, residual Pauli errors are below 0.1%, and bit-flip errors are extremely low (10⁻⁶). Surface code simulations confirm that this scheme provides a scalable path to rapidly suppressing errors in error-corrected systems. The work represents a key advance toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing. Results were published in *Nature* on August 5.

**Source:**
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10822-y

## DARPA Launches "It's About Time" Program to Establish Pilot Manufacturing Process for Optical Clocks

On August 6, DARPA launched the "It's About Time" program, aimed at establishing a pilot manufacturing process for optical clocks. The initiative builds on DARPA's ROCkN and OASIC programs, which advanced compact optical clocks while developing the manufacturing, testing, packaging, and integration practices required for large-scale deployment. IonQ, through its subsidiary Vector Atomic, will establish a production pipeline; the production facility is expected to be operational by mid-2027, with deliverable optical clock units anticipated approximately one year after completion.

**Source:**
https://www.darpa.mil/news/2026/its-about-time

## China's State Council Revises Integrated Circuit Layout-Design Protection Regulations, Incorporating Photonic Quantum Chips into Protection Scope for the First Time

On August 3, Premier Li Qiang signed State Council Order No. 842, promulgating the revised *Regulations on the Protection of Layout-Designs of Integrated Circuits*, effective October 15, 2026. This marks the first comprehensive revision of the regulations since their enactment in 2001—a span of 25 years—signaling a new phase in China's intellectual property protection regime for integrated circuits. The most notable breakthrough in this revision is the expansion of protection scope from traditional electronic integrated circuits to layout-designs of integrated circuits incorporating integrated photonic, quantum, and other functional technologies.

**Source:**
https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202608/content_7077399.htm

## Thailand Establishes Quantum Club Thailand to Support Quantum Technology Development

On August 3, the Bangkok Post reported that Thailand launched "Quantum Club Thailand," a national-level platform bringing together government, industry, research institutions, and quantum technology companies to jointly support quantum development. The initiative will focus on workforce development, applied research, industry adoption, and startup innovation, with programs including Quantum Academy Thailand, Quantum Industry Lab, and the Quantum Innovation Challenge. The platform will initially concentrate on quantum optimization, simulation and digital twins, quantum AI, and quantum-safe applications.

## Israel Launches National Quantum Computer Tender to Establish a Domestically Developed Quantum Computing Platform

On August 4, Israel launched "Project Nexus," a national tender aimed at establishing a domestically developed quantum computing platform. As the first major implementation step of its national AI strategy, the project is intended to strengthen technological sovereignty and support global competitiveness. The government stated that the quantum platform will support multiple quantum computing technologies developed in Israel, but did not disclose technical specifications, funding, timelines, or participating organizations. ## Russian Academy of Sciences Studies Reflection and Refraction Properties of a Laser-Driven 2D Quantum Well

This study investigates the scattering of weak probe waves by a laser-driven two-dimensional quantum well. Under optical excitation, the quantum well produces an oscillating two-dimensional electron plasma that exhibits Floquet scattering, analogous to a photonic time crystal, for obliquely incident probe waves. To first perturbative order, the reflected and transmitted radiation contain a main component at the unshifted probe frequency as well as up- and down-shifted satellite components. The down-shifted component propagates in reverse when the probe frequency is below the plasma oscillation frequency, transforming into surface waves under specific conditions. For s-polarized probes, the quantum well can support transverse-electric surface waves that cannot normally propagate freely. Results were published in *Physical Review Applied* on August 6.
